transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, thank you. Um, to be honest, what finally made me make an appointment is that I've started having these thoughts. I want to be clear right away that I don't have a plan to harm myself or anything like that. But I just keep catching myself thinking... that it would be simpler if I just didn't wake up tomorrow. And honestly, having thoughts like that scared me enough to come in and talk to someone.
Do you feel you might act on these thoughts today?

No, I don't. Like I mentioned a moment ago, I really don't have any actual plan to harm myself. I wouldn't do anything like that today, or at all. It's just that... well, having those thoughts in the first place, about how it would be simpler to just not wake up, that's what scared me enough to come in and get help. I don't want to act on them, I just want them to stop.
Have you been feeling depressed or down lately?

Yes, I have. Um... most days I feel as if a gray film has just settled over everything. Even when I’m doing simple things, like making a cup of tea or looking out at my garden, there’s this quiet heaviness in me. I keep trying to think my way through it, but I just can’t quite reason my way out of it.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It has been about eight months now. Um, I think it really started right around the time my brother's health and behavior changed so suddenly.
During these eight months, have you still been able to enjoy things you usually enjoy?

No, not really. I still set out my watercolor things sometimes... but I'll just sit there staring at the paper. Then I end up putting it all away because that pleasure I used to feel in the color and the light, it just doesn't seem to arrive anymore.
During these eight months, how has your energy been?

I think my energy has been mostly fine. Um... I haven't really noticed being more tired than usual. I still have the physical energy to do things around the house, I just... well, as I said, I just don't really have the interest. But physically, I wouldn't say my energy has really changed.
Do these feelings occur only when you are thinking about or dealing with your brother’s situation, or do they continue even when it is not on your mind?

They continue even when he isn't on my mind. Actually, most days I feel as if a... a gray film has settled over everything. Even when I’m just doing something simple, like making a cup of tea or looking out at my garden, there’s this quiet heaviness in me. I know I shouldn't feel that way in those everyday moments, but I just can’t quite reason my way out of it.
Have you been having trouble concentrating during these eight months?

No, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed any issues with that. I can still sit down and read a book, or follow a conversation without losing my train of thought. My mind doesn't really wander any more than it usually does. So... no, my concentration seems to be perfectly fine.
During these eight months, have you been feeling excessively guilty or worthless?

Yes, I have. Mostly guilt, I'd say. I just... I keep going back over my brother’s decline in my head. I keep telling myself that if I had been a better sister, or if I had just been more attentive, I would have noticed something was wrong sooner. I just feel like I could have prevented some of this from happening if I had paid closer attention.
How has your sleep been during these eight months?

It hasn't been very good, to be honest. Getting to sleep is... well, it's a bit uneven. I don't usually drift right off. And then I almost always wake up around three or four in the morning. 

Once I'm awake, my mind just starts going. I start thinking about all the phone calls I need to make, the forms to fill out, and just worrying about whether I handled things correctly with my brother's situation. Because of all that, by the time morning actually comes, I feel as if I’ve hardly rested at all.
Have you ever had a distinct period when your mood was unusually elevated or unusually irritable compared with your usual self?

No, I don't think so. I haven't ever felt like that. I mean, I can get a little frustrated sometimes with all the paperwork and phone calls lately, but... no, nothing unusual like being really hyper or excessively irritable. Just my normal self, really.
